title: C#
tagline: Modern C# and .NET, from console apps to real applications
description: Modern C# on .NET, from the first line to a complete, tested application. The course covers types, strings and control flow, methods, collections and LINQ, pattern matching, classes, records, interfaces and inheritance, generics, delegates and events, exceptions and resources, async and await, files and JSON, and how real applications are structured: projects and NuGet, unit tests, dependency injection and desktop UI, and finally the advanced language: operators and indexers, collections in depth, reflection and attributes, Span and performance, regular expressions, and async streams with channels, then LINQ in depth, every kind of pattern, generic math, dates and culture, and variance. Practice compiles and runs on .NET 9 from your browser.

milestones.title: First Steps
milestones.blurb: The .NET toolchain and your first program, variables and types, operators, strings and formatting, and control flow.

lessons.title: C# and .NET: Your First Program
lessons.summary: What C# and .NET are, how a program is compiled and run, the dotnet command-line tool, top-level statements, Console.WriteLine and ReadLine, comments, and reading compiler errors.

lessons.title: Variables and Types
lessons.summary: Declaring variables with explicit types and var, the built-in value types - int, long, double, decimal, bool, char - and string, constants, default values, value versus reference types, and converting between types with casts, Parse, TryParse and Convert.

lessons.title: Operators and Math
lessons.summary: Arithmetic and integer division, remainder, compound assignment and increment, comparison and logical operators with short-circuiting, the conditional operator, operator precedence, and the Math class for rounding, powers and roots.

lessons.title: Strings and Formatting
lessons.summary: Working with text - string literals, escapes, verbatim and raw strings, interpolation with format specifiers and alignment, the common string methods, comparing strings, characters, and building text efficiently with StringBuilder.

lessons.title: Control Flow
lessons.summary: Making decisions with if, else if and else, the switch statement and switch expressions, loops with while, do-while, for and foreach, break and continue, nested loops, and input loops that keep asking until the input is valid.

projects.title: A bank account at the console

milestones.title: Methods and Collections
milestones.blurb: Methods and parameters, arrays and lists, dictionaries and sets, LINQ, nullable types and pattern matching.

lessons.title: Methods and Parameters
lessons.summary: Writing methods with parameters and return values, expression-bodied methods, overloading, optional and named arguments, params arrays, ref, out and in parameters, local functions, recursion, and static methods in classes.

lessons.title: Arrays and Lists
lessons.summary: Fixed-size arrays and growable List<T> - creating, indexing, ranges and Index from the end, iterating, adding, inserting and removing, searching, sorting with comparisons, copying versus sharing, collection expressions, and two-dimensional and jagged arrays.

lessons.title: Dictionaries and Sets
lessons.summary: Dictionary<TKey, TValue> for lookups by key - adding, reading safely with TryGetValue, updating, counting and grouping, iterating key-value pairs - and HashSet<T> for unique values and set operations, with case-insensitive keys, sorted variants and queues and stacks.

lessons.title: LINQ
lessons.summary: Language Integrated Query - filtering, projecting and ordering with Where, Select, OrderBy and ThenBy, aggregates like Count, Sum, Average, Min and Max, First, Any and All, grouping with GroupBy and CountBy, ToDictionary, SelectMany, Distinct, Zip, deferred execution and query syntax.

lessons.title: Nullable Types and Pattern Matching
lessons.summary: null and nullable reference types, the warnings that catch null bugs, the operators ?. ?? and ??=, nullable value types like int?, tuples, and pattern matching with is, switch expressions, type, relational, logical, property and list patterns.

milestones.title: Object-Oriented C#
milestones.blurb: Classes and properties, records and structs, inheritance and polymorphism, interfaces, static members and extension methods.

lessons.title: Classes and Properties
lessons.summary: Defining classes with fields, constructors and methods, properties with get, set, init and validation, auto-properties and required members, primary constructors, access modifiers and encapsulation, object initializers, ToString, and reference semantics.

lessons.title: Records and Structs
lessons.summary: Records for data with value equality, positional records, with-expressions for non-destructive changes, deconstruction, record structs; structs as small value types, copying semantics, readonly structs, and choosing between class, record and struct.

lessons.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
lessons.summary: Deriving classes with a base class, calling base constructors, virtual and override, abstract classes and members, sealed, polymorphism through base-class references, protected members, type checks with is and as, and when composition is better than inheritance.

lessons.title: Interfaces
lessons.summary: Interfaces as contracts, implementing several interfaces, programming against interfaces instead of concrete classes, the built-in IComparable, IEquatable and IEnumerable, default interface methods, explicit implementation, and using interfaces to swap implementations and test code.

lessons.title: Static Members, Extension Methods and Namespaces
lessons.summary: Static fields, properties, methods and constructors, static classes, constants and readonly fields, extension methods that add methods to existing types, namespaces and using directives, file-scoped namespaces, global usings, and organising a project into files.

milestones.title: Generics, Delegates and Errors
milestones.blurb: Generics, delegates, lambdas and events, exceptions, IDisposable and using, and iterators with yield.

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.summary: Writing type-safe code that works for any type - generic methods and classes, type inference, constraints with where (class, struct, new(), interfaces, notnull), generic interfaces, default(T), covariance in IEnumerable and IReadOnlyList, and why generics beat object.

lessons.title: Delegates, Lambdas and Events
lessons.summary: Treating methods as values - delegate types, Func and Action, lambdas and method groups, closures that capture variables, higher-order methods, multicast delegates, and events for notifications with the EventHandler pattern, subscribing and unsubscribing safely.

lessons.title: Exceptions
lessons.summary: Throwing and catching exceptions, the common exception types, catch order and exception filters, finally, rethrowing with throw versus throw ex, custom exception classes with inner exceptions, guard clauses and ArgumentException helpers, and when to use Try methods or result types instead.

lessons.title: IDisposable and using
lessons.summary: Releasing files, connections and other resources on time - how the garbage collector works and what it does not do, IDisposable, using statements and declarations, try/finally underneath, implementing Dispose in your own classes, IAsyncDisposable, and scoped helpers built on using.

lessons.title: Iterators and yield
lessons.summary: How foreach works with IEnumerable and IEnumerator, writing iterators with yield return and yield break, lazy and infinite sequences, deferred execution and its pitfalls, writing your own LINQ-style extension methods, and implementing IEnumerable<T> on a collection class.

projects.title: A generic pair and a max helper

milestones.title: Async, Files and Data
milestones.blurb: Tasks and async/await, parallel work and cancellation, files and streams, JSON, and HTTP with HttpClient.

lessons.title: Tasks and async/await
lessons.summary: Asynchronous code in C# - why waiting should not block a thread, Task and Task<T>, async methods and await, running work in sequence or at the same time with Task.WhenAll and WhenAny, exceptions in async code, async void and why to avoid it, ValueTask, async streams with IAsyncEnumerable, and never blocking with .Result.

lessons.title: Parallel Work and Cancellation
lessons.summary: Using several cores and stopping work politely - Task.Run for CPU-bound work, Parallel.For and Parallel.ForEachAsync, limiting concurrency with SemaphoreSlim, thread safety with lock, Interlocked and concurrent collections, CancellationToken and CancellationTokenSource, timeouts, and progress reporting.

lessons.title: Files and Streams
lessons.summary: Reading and writing files with File's one-line helpers and their async versions, paths with Path, directories, StreamReader and StreamWriter for large files line by line, encodings, the Stream abstraction, handling IOException, and reading CSV safely.

lessons.title: JSON with System.Text.Json
lessons.summary: Converting objects to and from JSON with JsonSerializer - serialising records and collections, options for naming, indentation and enums, attributes like JsonPropertyName and JsonIgnore, deserialising safely with nullable results and validation, reading unknown JSON with JsonDocument and JsonNode, and saving settings files.

lessons.title: HTTP with HttpClient
lessons.summary: Calling web APIs - one shared HttpClient, GET and POST with JSON helpers, status codes and EnsureSuccessStatusCode, headers and authentication, query strings, timeouts and cancellation, retries for transient failures, typed API clients, and testing code that uses HTTP.

tasks.title: A service around an HTTP API

milestones.title: Building Applications
milestones.blurb: Solutions, projects and NuGet, unit testing, dependency injection and configuration, desktop UI, and a complete application.

lessons.title: Solutions, Projects and NuGet
lessons.summary: How real .NET code is organised - the .csproj file and its key settings, solutions with several projects, class libraries and project references, NuGet packages and versions, the dotnet CLI for building, testing, running and publishing, build configurations, and a sensible folder layout.

lessons.title: Unit Testing
lessons.summary: Writing automated tests with xUnit - test projects, Facts and Theories with InlineData, Arrange-Act-Assert, asserting values, collections and exceptions, testing async code, fakes for dependencies, what makes code testable, test naming, and how a test framework finds and runs tests with attributes and reflection.

lessons.title: Dependency Injection and Configuration
lessons.summary: Building applications from small services - constructor injection, the composition root, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection with singleton, scoped and transient lifetimes, the generic host, configuration from appsettings.json, environment variables and user secrets bound to options classes, logging with ILogger, and how a container resolves constructors.

lessons.title: Desktop UI and MVVM
lessons.summary: Building desktop applications with C# - the choices (WinForms, WPF, WinUI, Avalonia, .NET MAUI), event-driven UI and the UI thread, XAML and data binding, the MVVM pattern with INotifyPropertyChanged, ObservableCollection and ICommand, keeping the UI responsive with async, and testing view models without a window.

lessons.title: Project: A Complete Application
lessons.summary: Designing and building a whole application from the course's parts - a budget tracker with a domain library, commands parsed from input, services behind interfaces, JSON persistence with versions, reports with LINQ, error handling at the edges, tests, and where to go next with C#.

milestones.title: Advanced C#
milestones.blurb: Operator overloading and indexers, collections in depth, reflection and attributes, Span and performance, regular expressions and text, and async streams with channels.

lessons.title: Operators, Indexers and Conversions
lessons.summary: Making your own types feel built in - overloading arithmetic and comparison operators, equality done right, indexers with this[...], Index and Range support, implicit and explicit conversion operators, and when not to overload.

tasks.title: A sparse matrix with an indexer

lessons.title: Collections in Depth
lessons.summary: Choosing the right collection - Stack, Queue and PriorityQueue, LinkedList, SortedDictionary and SortedSet, read-only views, immutable and frozen collections, concurrent collections for threads, and what each operation costs.

lessons.title: Reflection and Attributes
lessons.summary: Programs that look at themselves - Type objects, reading properties and methods with reflection, creating objects and calling methods by name, attributes as labels on code, writing and reading your own attributes, and why source generators replace much of this today.

lessons.title: Span, Memory and Performance
lessons.summary: Writing fast C# without unsafe code - value types and the stack, Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<T> as views over arrays and strings, slicing without copying, stackalloc, ArrayPool for reusing buffers, ref struct rules, and measuring before optimising.

lessons.title: Regular Expressions and Text
lessons.summary: Finding and transforming text - the Regex class, patterns, groups and named groups, Matches and Replace with a MatchEvaluator, options, timeouts, [GeneratedRegex] for speed, and culture-aware comparison, formatting and normalisation of strings.

lessons.title: Async Streams and Channels
lessons.summary: Data that arrives over time - IAsyncEnumerable with yield return and await foreach, cancellation with [EnumeratorCancellation], System.Threading.Channels for producers and consumers, bounded channels and back-pressure, and pipelines of async stages.

tasks.title: A worker pool on a channel

projects.title: A command console driven by attributes

milestones.title: C# in Depth
milestones.blurb: LINQ joins and deferred execution, every kind of pattern, generic math with static abstract members, dates, times and culture, and variance in generics.

lessons.title: LINQ in Depth
lessons.summary: The rest of LINQ - query syntax and how it maps to methods, joining two sequences with Join and GroupJoin, flattening with SelectMany, Aggregate, Zip, Chunk and the By methods, ToLookup, set operations, and the deferred execution rules that decide when a query actually runs.

lessons.title: Pattern Matching in Depth
lessons.summary: Every pattern C# can match - type, constant and relational patterns, and, or and not, property patterns with nested and extended forms, positional patterns with Deconstruct, list patterns with slices, var patterns, switch expressions that the compiler checks for completeness, and how to keep complex matches readable.

lessons.title: Generic Math and Static Abstract Members
lessons.summary: Writing one method that works for every number type - why generics could not do arithmetic before, the INumber<T> family of interfaces, T.Zero, T.One and T.CreateChecked, static abstract and static virtual interface members, defining operators in your own generic interfaces, and when generic math is worth it.

lessons.title: Dates, Times and Culture
lessons.summary: Getting time and formatting right in .NET - DateTime and its Kind, DateTimeOffset for moments, DateOnly and TimeOnly for calendar values, TimeSpan and date arithmetic, time zones with TimeZoneInfo, TimeProvider for testable code, and CultureInfo for numbers and dates that look right in every country and parse the same everywhere.

lessons.title: Variance and Advanced Generics
lessons.summary: The finer points of generics - why a List<Cat> is not a List<Animal>, covariance with out and contravariance with in, which built-in interfaces and delegates are variant, writing variant interfaces of your own, default(T), static data per closed generic type, generic caches, and constraints for enums, delegates and unmanaged types.
